newsitem.title: POLAND: BIG wants Gdanski merger by Oct.
newsitem.headline: BIG wants Gdanski merger by Oct.

text.p: Polish Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) would like to conclude its planned merger with 63.4-percent-owned subsidiary Bank Gdanski SA by the end of September, BIG's spokesman said on Tuesday.
Wojciech Kaczorowski said the bank would like to merge with Gdanski before BIG's financial year ends on September 30.
"We would like to enter our new financial year as one bank from the legal point of view, but surely the process of merging operations will last longer, " he said. @

Kaczorowski said at the end of June shareholders of both banks would vote on the merger, which would be concluded by BIG taking all the assets of Gdanski and issuing new shares for Gdanski's shareholders. Gdanski's shares would then be retired.
He said the parity of the share offer for shareholders had yet to be set.
Kaczorowski said, however, the merger and its time-table would also depend on the Polish Securities Commission and Anti-Monopoly Office approval. @
In February BIG became a majority owner of Bank Gdanski after it doubled its stake to about 63 percent, buying shares from the state treasury.
Kaczorowski said the merged banks would rank seventh in the ranking of the largest Polish banks according to total assets. Currently Gdanski ranks 12th and BIG 14th.
According to own funds the merged bank would move to fifth position, from Gdanski's ninth and BIG's 14th.
